messages.body_plain:
The question of plotting groups within multiple panels comes up quite
regularly, so I thought it worthwhile to give an example. 

Extra control within a panel function is provided by the subscripts and
groups arguments. subscripts has length equal to the data going into the
panel whereas subscripts has the length of the original data (before
subsetting). The arguments have to be called "subscripts" and "groups"
otherwise an error occurs. 

This example plots some data and does separate fits to groups within panels.
The strips are turned off and the factor levels displayed in the panel
instead.

df <- expand.grid(fac1=letters[1:2],x=seq(0,1,.1),fac2=LETTERS[1:4])
df$y  <- df$x*codes(df$fac1)+codes(df$fac2)*df$x^2+rnorm(nrow(df))/10
xyplot(y~x|fac2,
        groups=fac1,
        data=df,
        strip = F,
        panel=function(x,y,subscripts,groups) {
                panel.superpose(x,y,subscripts,groups)
                for(g in as.character(unique(groups[subscripts]))) {
                        sub <- groups[subscripts] == g
                        fit <- lm(y~x+I(x^2),subset=sub)
                        ord <- order(x[sub])
                        lines(x[sub][ord],fitted(fit)[ord])
                        text(0,6,as.character(df$fac2)[subscripts][1])
                }
        }
)

Below is a modification of Karl's example:

galaxy.df2 <- data.frame(angle = rep(galaxy[1:100,3],3), velocity =
rep(galaxy[1:100,5],3), y = as.vector(as.matrix(galaxy[1:100,c(1,2,4)])),
meas = factor(rep(1:3,rep(100,3)),labels=names(galaxy[1:100,c(1,2,4)])))

xyplot(velocity ~ y | meas,
groups=angle,data=galaxy.df2,scales=list(x="free"),strip=F,
               panel=function(x,y,subscripts,groups) {
                panel.superpose(x,y,subscripts,groups)
                for(g in as.character(unique(groups[subscripts]))) {
                        sub <- groups[subscripts] == g
                        fit <- lm(y~x+I(x^2),subset=sub)
                        ord <- order(x[sub])
                        lines(x[sub][ord],fitted(fit)[ord])
                        meas <- as.character(galaxy.df2$meas)[subscripts][1]
                        right <- meas=="north.south"
                        text(par("usr")[if(right) 2 else
1],par("usr")[4]-10,meas,adj=right)
                }
        }
)

messages.body_plain:
On Thu, 30 Aug 2001, Patricia Stephenson wrote:

> I would like to use the "message of reason for termination" produced by
> nlminb in an "if" statement so that I can take different actions
> depending on the message returned (i.e. if (nlminb()$message=="FALSE
> CONVERGENCE") {}). The "if" statement will not allow me to do this
> because sometimes the message returned by nlminb is "NULL" which
> causes an error and returns NA when used in an "if" statement.
>
> What does "NULL" mean and how can I create conditional statements that
> will not always return NAs and errors since they are performing
> calculations on a "NULL" value?

I would suggest

mess <- nlminb()$message
if(is.null(mess)) mess <- "unknown"
....

In the version I am looking at it comes from

        msg <- switch(temp$iv[1] - 2,
                "X CONVERGENCE",
                "RELATIVE FUNCTION CONVERGENCE",
                "BOTH X AND RELATIVE FUNCTION CONVERGENCE",
                "ABSOLUTE FUNCTION CONVERGENCE",
                "SINGULAR CONVERGENCE",
                "FALSE CONVERGENCE",
                "FUNCTION EVALUATION LIMIT REACHED",
                "ITERATION LIMIT REACHED",
                stop("ERROR : INVALID OUTPUT CODE 11"),
                stop("ERROR : INVALID OUTPUT CODE 12"),
                stop("ERROR : INVALID OUTPUT CODE 13"),
                stop("LIV is too small"),
                stop("LV is too small"),
                stop("ERROR : INVALID OUTPUT CODE 17"),
                stop("negative component in scale vector"),
                default("cannot complete optimization"))

and so you get NULL if the error code is less than 3 or more than 16.
And for 16 you will get an error, there is no default() function.
Only someone with the source code can tell you what those numbers mean.

So that's a bug report for Insightful: there are internal error codes
not being handled correctly.  Please follow this up by telling them the
version of S-PLUS you used, and if possible a test case which gives NULL.

>  1  1  1
>  2  1  1
>  3  1  1
>  4  2  1
>  5  0  0
>  6  1  0
>  7  0  0
>  8  1  1
>  9  1  1
> according to values in the column labelled "V3".
> Every time I get to the first in a
> sequence of identical values in "V3", I would like
> to extract that row to obtain the following
>    V3 V5
>  1  1  1
>  4  2  1
>  5  0  0
>  6  1  0
>  7  0  0
>  8  1  1
>

There seemed to be three different short flavors of doing it (listed
in no particular order). All involve prepending a dummy term to the vectpor
in order to ensure that the first observation is selected.

1. Using length():

   last <- c(-99,temp$V3[-length(temp$V3)])
   temp[temp$V3 != last,]

2. Using rle():

   > temp <-
   +   cbind(c(1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1),
   +         c(1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1))
   > temp
        [,1] [,2] 
        [1,]    1    1
        [2,]    1    1
        [3,]    1    1
        [4,]    2    1
        [5,]    0    0
        [6,]    1    0
        [7,]    0    0
        [8,]    1    1
        [9,]    1    1
        > 
        > 
        > indexes <- 1 + cumsum(rle(temp[, 1])$length)
        > indexes <- c(1, indexes[-length(indexes)])
        > indexes
        [1] 1 4 5 6 7 8
        > temp[indexes, ]
             [,1] [,2] 
             [1,]    1    1
             [2,]    2    1
             [3,]    0    0
             [4,]    1    0
             [5,]    0    0
             [6,]    1    1

3. Using diff():

   foo<-c(T,diff(temp$V3)!=0)
   new.frame<-temp[foo,]

Thank you very much,
Anna

messages.subject_clean: Bug in symbols() with matrix argument?
messages.body_plain:
Hi. I want to use symbols() to draw a bunch (technically, a "herd") of
circles simultaneously using S-Plus 2000 Professional release 3 under NT 4.0

The help says, "The coordinates can be given by two arguments that are
vectors, or by a single argument x which is... a matrix with 2 columns..."

So this ought to work, right?

> plot (1:5)  # Set up a plot
> mat <- matrix (c(3, 4, 3, 4), nrow=2) # Here are the locations of the
circles I want
> symbols (x = mat, circles = rep (.2, 2), add=T, inches=F) # Draw, pardner
Error in symbols: Number of symbol parameters must match number of points

Huh? There are two symbol parameters and "mat" is a matrix with two rows.
How about this?

> symbols (mat[,1], mat[,2], circles = rep (.2, 2), add=T, inches=F)

This works fine. Is this a bug? Or a "bug" in the documentation?

Thanks,
Sam Buttrey
buttrey at nps.navy.mil
